validity.recommendation: keep as operating; existence, classification and non-duplicate status are all well documented
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independently of GEM/wiki: EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (Historical Projects 1996-2024 tab, downloaded and read locally) lists 'Westbrook Xpress Project Phase 3' verbatim as a completed FERC-jurisdictional expansion project of Portland Natural Gas Transmission System -- Completed Date 2021-10-21, Year In Service 2021, Additional Capacity 18 MMcf/d, States QU/NH/ME, Authority FERC. This matches the sheet's Capacity (18.00 MMcf/d) and StartYear1 (2021) exactly. A second, genuinely independent trade-press source (Gas Compression Magazine, 2020-02-12, verified via its Wayback capture since the live site 403s scripted clients) confirms PNGTS was 'seeking FERC approval to begin Phase II and Phase III' of the Westbrook XPress Project at the Westbrook Compressor Station (Cumberland County, Maine) as of Feb 2020, with a combined Northern-system (Pittsburg NH to Westbrook ME) capacity increase of 80,998 Mcf/d for the two phases together -- consistent within rounding with EIA's per-phase split (Phase 2 = 63 + Phase 3 = 18 = 81 MMcf/d). CLASSIFICATION correct: this is a compression-only capacity expansion on an existing FERC-regulated interstate gas transmission mainline (adding a compressor unit at the existing Westbrook, ME compressor station), not new pipe and not a gathering/feeder line -- LengthKnown=0/blank Diameter is the RULE for this kind of project, not a defect (see fills). NO DUPLICATE: distinct from its sibling phases on the roster -- P2588 'Portland Xpress Project Phase 3' (EIA: completed 2020-10-28, 24 MMcf/d, matches sheet's 24.00) and P2631 'Westbrook Xpress Project Phase 2' (EIA: completed 2021-10-21, 63 MMcf/d, matches sheet's 63.00) are each separately, distinctly named and dated in the same EIA dataset -- P3280/P2588/P2631 are three genuinely separate FERC-authorized project phases, not a relabeled duplicate of one another. CAVEAT: ownership of the whole PNGTS system changed in 2024 -- see the attribution concern below, which is the one open issue on this row.

validity.recommendation: update Owner1/Owner2 off TC Energy (61.70%) / Northern New England Investment Co (38.30%) -- PNGTS was sold in 2024 and those owners no longer hold the asset
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current Owner1='TC Energy'/61.70%, Owner2='Northern New England Investment Co'/38.30% are STALE. Per TC Energy's own news release (2024-03-04, 'TC Energy announces sale of Portland Natural Gas Transmission System', verified via its Wayback capture since the live URL now 404s post-sale), TC Energy and its partner Northern New England Investment Company, Inc. (a subsidiary of Energir L.P.) entered a purchase-and-sale agreement to sell 100% of PNGTS to BlackRock, through a fund managed by its Diversified Infrastructure business, and investment funds managed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners, for a gross purchase price of US$1.14 billion (including assumption of $250M in Senior Notes) -- the cash proceeds were to be split pro-rata per the OLD ownership stakes (TC Energy 61.7%/Energir 38.3%), not the buyers' split, and no source found discloses the BlackRock/Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners split. Independently, PNGTS's own site (pngts.com, press release dated 2024-08-15, 'Portland Natural Gas Transmission System To Operate As A Standalone Company Under Industry Veteran') confirms the transaction closed: 'PNGTS has completed its transition into a standalone company. Previously a subsidiary of TC Energy Corporation and Northern New England Investment Company, Inc., a subsidiary of Energir L.P. ...' and names Bill Yardley (ex-Enbridge EVP) as the new standalone company's CEO. This is TWO independent origins (TC Energy's own release naming the specific buyers, and PNGTS's own post-closing release confirming closing) agreeing that TC Energy/Energir no longer own the asset as of 2024-08-15 -- well after the row's LastUpdated of 2023-08-03. I could not find a source stating the BlackRock/Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners ownership split percentages, so Owner1%/Owner2% are left unproposed rather than guessed. Operator is also proposed to change to 'Portland Natural Gas Transmission System' itself (the standalone operating company, per its own site and the Aug-2024 release) rather than TC Energy, since PNGTS no longer has a TC Energy operator relationship post-sale. This finding applies to the whole PNGTS system, not just this segment -- flagging for the orchestrator to route to every PNGTS row's Owner/Operator units (P0242, P2588, P2631 share the same operators_owners entity).
